text:
Tip: A common accessibility blind spot in modern work culture is "calendar overload." We often assume everyone has the same capacity for cognitive load or sensory processing. When we fill schedules with back-to-back meetings, we ignore the needs of neurodivergent colleagues who may require more transition time or sensory breaks to function effectively. 

True accessibility means building buffer zones into our schedules, not just ensuring meetings are captioned. It’s time to rethink how we respect everyone's mental bandwidth.
